newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Ben Bella party to boycott poll.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Ben Bella party to boycott poll.

text.p: The Movement for Democracy in Algeria (MDA), a legal opposition group led by former president Ahmed Ben Bella, will boycott Algeria's June 5 parliamentary elections, Algerian state-run radio said on Sunday.
The radio quoted MDA secretary general Khaled Bensmail announcing the boycott.
The MDA demanded President Liamine Zeroual opens talks with opposition groups, including the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), to end violence before holding elections.
Zeroual had held talks with a range of politicians over the elections but ignored calls for dialogue with the banned FIS.

All other legal opposition parties are to take part in the elections except anti-Islamist Ettahaddi which wants the government to ban all Islamist parties. Algeria's two legal Islamist groups, Hamas and Nahda, are to participate.
The banned FIS called on Algerians last week to boycott the parliamentary elections, which it said would be neither free nor fair.

Algeria has been without an elected parliament since January 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS had a huge lead. About 60,000 people have died since then in violence between Moslem guerrillas and government forces.
